findings.title: Fallible texture read accepts host types that panic at the final byte cast
findings.scenario: An initialized 1x1 R8Unorm texture/view read::<u32> yields one packed byte then bytemuck::cast_slice panics with slop; nonempty read::<()> also fails. Vec<u8> allocation does not contractually satisfy arbitrary T alignment even when byte count divides T.
findings.contract: A Result<Vec<T>> read should reject unsupported host layout without panic and copy bytes into an aligned, initialized Vec<T>.
findings.connected_repair: Reuse the existing canonical buffer Readback<T> host admission/copy owner; make its required crate scope available, without duplicating typed allocation/initialization logic. Preserve View empty-first before host admission.
acceptance: Nonempty ZST/partial elements return existing concrete host-layout error before native work.
Aligned destination handles unaligned input bytes and preserves all original native-endian bits.
Packed output excludes every padded GPU row and preserves z-major then row-major order.

findings.title: Texture staging volume narrows through unchecked u32 arithmetic
findings.scenario: Texture3d::read computes padded_row*height*depth as u32 then casts to u64. A 1024-cubed R32Float volume has 2^32 bytes, within source dimension bounds when the provider admits the allocation; debug panics or release wraps before the native buffer limit can reject it. This does not claim any current device can allocate it. A larger custom 2D device may expose the analogous 16384-square RGBA32 case; baseline 8192 2D alone does not prove that scenario.
findings.contract: Rows, full padded staging volume, packed bytes and host addresses must be related in checked wide byte units before allocation/copy/slicing.
findings.connected_repair: One texture transfer-layout aggregate, native extent+pixel format at admission, BufferByteLength/Offset for byte semantics, checked row alignment/native-u32 and host-usize narrowing. Reuse SDK alignment constant. Check copy range against actual mapped extent; do not invent broader constructor/schema migrations.
acceptance: Checked padded and packed u64 products; checked native row and usize conversions retain actual narrowing causes.
No u32 volume/row-index multiplication before widening.
Queue upload rows stay tight, encoder copy rows stay 256-aligned; full padded allocation is permitted though SDK copy omits trailing last-row padding.

findings.title: Texture map/read progress loses concrete errors and lacks canonical request ownership
findings.scenario: Native callback Err becomes a formatted String, oneshot cancellation becomes a generic String, Poll failure is discarded; wasm erases even map detail. create_buffer and map_async immediate native validation also occur outside observe_validation; a synchronous map failure can route through the device sink before the function reports its callback error.
findings.contract: Keep actual native, BufferAsyncError, PollError and Canceled values, fail at the earliest observed boundary and clean this private request without replacing its primary error.
findings.connected_repair: Reuse canonical MappingRequest, BufferReadError, context.observe_validation and callback_progress; add only the separately owned nonblocking texture completion behavior. Own cleanup before scope result inspection, including synchronous callback. Preserve existing Buffer::read explicit-wait method.
acceptance: Ready-first callback outcome/cancellation precedes a later Poll; pending polls retain actual errors.
Texture native progress retains 1ms async cadence; no added Wait, including borrowed context; browser yields and may drive enabled non-WebGPU providers.
Successful view drops before unmap. Error/cancellation/unwind reset only owned private request; cleanup-only native scope no wait, no primary-error replacement.
No unconditional unmap on unrelated external aliases, no fake SDK map/device state query, no new global mapping lock.

findings.title: Texture upload Result boundaries miss immediate native queue validation
findings.scenario: For an initialized positive-size R32Float texture, write(&[]) reaches SDK queue source-byte bounds validation; queue errors route through its sink immediately. These functions return Ok if that handler continues, or panic under default handling, rather than returning the actual available native cause. The same boundary exists on image/cube uploads after packing.
findings.contract: Owned native validation policy must observe queue write at the actual immediate boundary, after conversion/layout; do not rely on a later submit scope.
findings.connected_repair: Wrap only queue.write_texture in context.observe_validation after fallible conversion and checked tight layout; existing context device/queue precondition and borrowed/browser handler policy remain. All five source call sites must be migrated together.
acceptance: Actual available native cause enters the owning error chain; no message flattening.
No new GPU completion wait or waiting ValidationScope for queue writes.
Do not impose 256-byte alignment on queue writes, require exact source size when SDK accepts trailing data, or change existing colour/packing behavior.
Cube per-face upload does not promise atomic rollback of already queued earlier faces.

findings.title: Image float decoding relies on byte-vector alignment
findings.scenario: read_image reads Vec<u8> then casts it to &[f32] for Rgba32Float/R32Float. This reintroduces an alignment requirement that the byte vector contract does not guarantee after TR1 is fixed.
findings.contract: Image decoding must preserve native-endian float values without borrowing f32 from an alignment-one allocation.
findings.connected_repair: Use exact four-byte chunks and f32::from_ne_bytes, preserving clamp/round/greyscale/alpha and format decisions. This is not a new Image schema or colour-policy rewrite.
acceptance: Complete float byte chunks decode in existing native endian order; successful numerical operations/formats unchanged.
No mapped view held across host allocation and no new float alignment assumption.

Do not wait on GPU in cleanup, do not leave a native ErrorScopeGuard across await, and do not infer arbitrary alias map ownership.

scheduling: Texture reads currently use ready-first native try_recv then nonblocking Poll plus 1ms async sleep; preserve cadence with canonical polling completion entry.
Canonical Buffer::read complete() explicitly Waits; do not replace texture behavior by calling it without a consciously changed contract.
Browser WebGPU progresses automatically; canonical browser callback also drives non-WebGPU providers and yields zero timer turns.
Borrowed false/browser perform no new validation wait or verdict scope; available native poll/map errors remain results.
Submission finish and queue boundaries remain canonical immediate no-wait context.submit.
Native Poll(Poll) may return no timeout on some providers; do not infer an observed runtime failure. Still retain every actual Result error rather than discard.
publication: Readback has no shared result cache; errors return no successful partially initialized Vec<T>.
Image upload creates private candidate before write; observe immediate write before returning it. Cube multiple uploads are not rollback-atomic.
Raw render/cube paths continue existing producer/submission semantics; no texture readback success certifies earlier ignored producing error, later writes or global GPU health.
